validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #51 collects four non-blocking findings the review of PR #50 raised and approved despite. Three are in the two sqlite test files PR #50 touched; the fourth is a PR-metadata nit. I reproduced each against the default branch before planning, as the ticket asks.

(1) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:35 — the afterEach added by PR #50 calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which restores every spy the file holds, including the global.fetch spy that patchFetchForSqlJS installs in the top-level beforeAll (index.test.ts:17, via vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch') at mocks/util.ts:71). My probe appended to the describe printed 'PROBE fetch isMock=false' with line 35 present and 'PROBE fetch isMock=true' with that one line removed. The suite stays green (9 passed) because init() runs once in the beforeAll and sql.js caches the compiled wasm, so this is latent rather than live — exactly as the review said. The fix the review proposed (re-arm the patch per test) works: patchFetchForSqlJS is a vi.spyOn(...).mockImplementation(...), so calling it again is idempotent, and with a beforeEach re-arm my same probe printed isMock=true and the suite stayed green.

The review also noted this leaves the file differing from its sibling fs/index.test.ts:20, which installs the same beforeAll fetch patch and was left alone. I checked why the sibling needs nothing: its afterEach (fs/index.test.ts:28-30) calls only sqlite._getModule().reset_filesystem() and never vi.restoreAllMocks(), so its fetch patch survives every test. The sibling is not a counterexample — it is the shape that has no bug. The divergence the review flagged is therefore correct after the fix, not a leftover.

(2) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.test.ts:143 — the comment block at lines 142-144 says `expect(handles).toHaveLength(0)` is 'above'. That assertion is at line 151, after teardown() at 148. grep confirms the only two occurrences of the string are the comment at 143 and the assertion at 151, in that order. One word is wrong.

(3) REPRODUCED. packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:29-30 — the comment PR #50 rewrote promises the afterEach 'would skip the cleanup and leave an open handle and a mocked console.log behind for the next test'. grep confirms 10 `await openDatabase()` calls (lines 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 341, 344, 382) but handles.push only at 342 and 345, both inside the one 'once per database handle' test. So the mock half is true for every test; the handle half is true for one test of nine. The comment overstates. The review explicitly scopes the fix to not overstating the comment rather than pushing in the eight other tests, and I agree — see out_of_scope.

(4) NOT A CODE CHANGE. PR #50's title lacks the mandatory `[AI]` prefix (.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md). PR #50 is MERGED (mergedAt 2026-10-03T14:41:18Z), so there is no diff to carry this fix: the rule is enforced when a PR is opened, and .github/** is a forbidden path. The review itself notes every recent PR (37, 39, 40, 49) shares this shape, which makes it a pipeline-wide habit and not this ticket's code. Deferred to a human with the reason recorded.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #50 added a blanket vi.restoreAllMocks() to index.test.ts's afterEach and, separately, wrote two comments that claim more than the code does. The blanket restore reaches beyond the console spy AC-1 targeted, because vi.restoreAllMocks() is file-scoped rather than spy-scoped; the comments were written from the shape of the teardown rather than from what each test actually registers.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three small edits across the two files PR #50 touched, plus one regression test that fails without the fix.

The fetch patch moves from once-per-file to once-per-test. Hoist the existing baseURL template literal to module scope (it is currently computed inside the beforeAll), keep patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) in the beforeAll where init({ baseURL }) needs it, and add a beforeEach that calls patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL) again. patchFetchForSqlJS is vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...), so re-spying a restored global is idempotent and the afterEach's blanket restore can no longer outrun it. This is the smaller of the two fixes the review offered — the other, narrowing the restore to the console spy alone, would mean hand-tracking the console spy and would break the deliberate mirroring of index.electron.test.ts's teardown().

A new test at the end of the describe asserts vi.isMockFunction(globalThis.fetch) is true. I verified both directions: appended to the unmodified file it fails with 'expected false to be true', and passes once the beforeEach re-arm is in. It must not be placed first — without the fix fetch is still patched during whichever test runs before the first afterEach, so a first-positioned assertion would pass for the wrong reason and be vacuous under -t filtering. A comment on the test must say so, matching the existing convention in index.electron.test.ts:61-66.

The two comment corrections are wording only. In index.test.ts:29-30 the comment is split so the mock half and the handle half carry their true scopes. In index.electron.test.ts:143 'above' becomes 'below'.

No production code changes. No new dependency. No behaviour change to anything outside the test files.

risks: The beforeEach re-arm is a new hook running before all ten tests in index.test.ts. patchFetchForSqlJS is a vi.spyOn(global, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...), so the second and later calls reinstall the same mock on an already-restored global; if that ever stopped being true the suite would fail loudly on the new assertion rather than silently.

The re-arm only touches global.fetch within this one test file. vitest isolates files by default, so it cannot leak into fs/index.test.ts, which runs in the same vitest.web.config.ts project. fs/index.test.ts is deliberately left alone: its afterEach never calls vi.restoreAllMocks().

Touching only comments in index.electron.test.ts means that file's runtime behaviour is unchanged; the only risk is a bad find-and-replace landing the wrong 'above' or 'below'. AC-3 pins the direction.

No path in forbidden_paths is touched: .sdlc/memory/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md, docs/ui.md, .github/** and .sdlc/** are all outside files[]. In particular the [AI] PR-title rule lives in .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, which no ticket may change — that is why finding 4 is deferred.
No new host is contacted and no new dependency is added, so env.api_allowlist is unaffected.

The review notes PRs 37, 39, 40 and 49 all share this shape, so it is a pipeline-wide habit in how PRs are opened. A human can rename the merged PR if they want the history to read correctly. The PR this ticket produces must carry the prefix.

Pushing handles.push(db) into the eight tests of index.test.ts that call openDatabase() without registering (lines 42, 71, 111, 154, 199, 220, 261, 382). The review explicitly scopes this out and this ticket does the same: eight unclosed in-memory sql.js handles inside a test process that exits minutes later is not a leak worth a diff. This ticket corrects the comment instead — the reviewer's stated fix.
Making the handle leak visible at all, e.g. asserting no sql.js handle survives the suite. Nothing currently observes it and adding an observer would be a new mechanism for a non-defect.
Any change to production code. The fetch patch and the teardown are test-only; nothing under packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.ts is touched.

assumptions: main is the base the implementer branches from, and the three code findings still hold there — reproduced on this checkout after yarn install, not from the reviewer's evidence.

patchFetchForSqlJS remains idempotent (vi.spyOn(...).mockImplementation with no restore inside it). If someone later makes it stateful, the beforeEach re-arm breaks and the new test is what catches it.
vitest isolates test files by default, so a beforeEach in index.test.ts cannot affect fs/index.test.ts running in the same project. If isolation were ever disabled, AC-5's fs run would show it.
The comment conventions in these files are load-bearing — index.electron.test.ts:129-137 argues at length about a test's position — so new comments here are expected to carry that reasoning.
